notes:
VERDICT: FAIL. The two attempt-2 majors are fixed, but the fix broke two locked features - the fourth time this pattern has occurred on this project.

WHAT WAS FIXED. (1) Vertical welt LENGTH, the headline fault: 3.81-3.85 waistband-depths in attempt 2, now 4.619 against the drawing's 4.552, a 1.5% match. Both endpoints landed too: top gap 0.523 vs 0.532 drawn, bottom gap 5.140 vs 5.082. (2) Composition, substantially: the subject now covers 51.1% of frame height (was 35%) and carries 2.02x the hip welt's length and 3.2x its ink-area, where in attempt 2 the two pockets were of literally equal visual area. Downgraded major to minor - what remains is only that the subject sits at 39.4% frame width, unmoved from attempt 2.

WHAT BROKE. The regeneration halved the hip welt's strip depth (0.338 -> 0.143 normalised, locked entry 6) and narrowed the vertical welt strip further (0.231 -> 0.209, locked entry 4, whose text explicitly said "Do not narrow or widen the strip when fixing the length"). Both are majors by the regression rule. The hip welt one is the more serious in substance: at 0.143 it reads as a jetted slit, and "welt, not jetted" is the entire selling point of this option, so the frame now contradicts itself.

CALIBRATION - how I know the hip-welt reading is real and not a convention change. I measured attempt 2 with my own pipeline first and recovered 0.334 against the locked 0.338, which fixes the convention as "the two strong lines bounding the lit strip face". Applying that same convention to attempt 3 gives 0.143. A third, normaliser-free check agrees: hip-welt depth divided by vertical-welt strip width is 1.32 in the drawing, 1.43 in attempt 2, 0.64 here.

FORESHORTENING RULED OUT. Attempt 3 is a tighter, more turned crop (waistband depth grew from 106.8 to 128.1px). Turning about a vertical axis compresses HORIZONTAL dimensions. The hip welt's strip depth is a near-vertical dimension sharing an axis with the waistband-depth landmark, so foreshortening cannot account for a 57% loss. The hip welt's LENGTH loss (-29%) is horizontal and I therefore scored that minor, not major.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE - what I checked and what I threw away.
1. Landmark validated first. Waistband depth: in the drawing the two edges are genuinely parallel (fitted slopes -0.10543 and -0.10547 over 650 sampled columns) giving a constant 102.99px perpendicular. In the render the band is an ARC, not a line, so I refused a single global value and fitted it locally twice - 128.09px under the vertical welt (x=230..470, seam resid 0.90px) and 120.10px under the hip welt (x=600..765, resid 0.97px) - and used each where it applies.
2. Span checked, not cropped. The welt edges were traced over a y=210..860 window; the feature occupies y=226..815, leaving 16px of headroom above and 45px below, so the endpoints are real fades and not window walls. The endpoint fade was then independently confirmed by locating the two horizontal end caps directly (top cap centre y=226.33 strength 38.9; bottom cap centre y=817.74 strength 27.2).
3. Saturation checked. The bottom cap was verified to die out by y=823 with nothing below it, so 815 is not a clipped boundary.
4. DISCARDED READING 1: the red annotation's PCA minor-axis extent, 46.40px. That is the outer envelope of a 17.4px-thick marker stroke, not the garment; using it would have made the render look 42% too narrow. The correct comparable is stroke-centreline to stroke-centreline, 26.0px, measured at eight separate heights (26.0-26.5).
5. DISCARDED READING 2: subtracting one stroke thickness from that PCA minor extent (giving 29.0px / 0.282) - the rounded end caps inflate the minor extent, so this is also wrong. Direct centreline gap stands.
6. DISCARDED READING 3: reading the hip welt's depth as line1-to-line3 (33px / 0.26). Line 3 is a shadow below the fold, not an edge - the attempt-2 calibration and the drawing both show a two-line strip with a lit face between. Shadow inside a fold is not an edge.
7. NOT MEASURABLE - locked entry 8. "Distance from the right silhouette edge, vertical welt : horizontal welt = 2.72 drawing / 2.80 render" cannot be re-verified: the garment now bleeds off the right frame edge continuously from y=470 to y=840, so there is no right silhouette at the vertical welt's height. I have NOT counted this as a loss (I have no evidence the placement moved) but it is now unverifiable, and I substituted a crease-normalised reading: welt-centre-to-crease 0.568 depths in the render vs 0.655 drawn (0.87 ratio, better than attempt 2's 0.68). Per the standing caveat that the freehand sketch is inconsistent to about +/-30% on horizontal secondary features, I raised no finding on it.
8. NO CENTIMETRES. The illustration carries no printed dimension callout, so no real-world size is recoverable. Every figure above is a ratio against waistband depth or a dimensionless aspect ratio.
9. Belt loop count reported as 3 + 1 descending seam in both, at MEDIUM confidence only - the drawing's leftmost loop still shares a stroke with the leg silhouette and cannot be cleanly separated. Unchanged caveat from attempt 2.
10. Orientation delta widened slightly, from 0.93 deg to about 1.4 deg (render 89.7 deg welt-to-seam vs drawing 88.24 deg). I tested five seam-fit windows (x=200..480) and the render figure is stable at 89.5-89.8 deg. Since the drawing's own waistband fit carries a 4.05px residual over 650px, a 0.5 deg shift is inside the drawing's noise floor and the essential property - perpendicular to the waistband, i.e. vertical - is unambiguously held. Marked HELD, not lost, with the number updated.

RESOLUTION. 880 x 1168, byte-identical dimensions to attempt 2, so the attempt-3 correction block's upscale precondition is unmet and write-back is blocked on that ground alone. But resolution is NOT the binding limit here: the two majors are geometry errors of 17% and 57% that are fully visible and measurable at 880px and would be identically wrong at 4K. Raise resolution on the same pass as the geometry fix, not instead of it.

RECOMMENDATION: regenerate. Exactly three changes and nothing else - (a) widen the vertical welt strip by about 20% to 0.252 waistband-depths WITHOUT touching its length or either endpoint, (b) restore the hip welt's strip depth to 0.33 waistband-depths, roughly double, keeping its current angle, (c) shift framing right by about 90px and raise output resolution. Everything in the new lockedFeatures list is correct now; a regeneration that loses the 4.619 length, the 89.7 deg orientation, the raised-welt lighting signature or the 51% frame-height subject dominance is a worse image than this one.

FILE SAFETY: no files were written under data-store/, public/images/generated/, or .craft-pipeline/. All working files are in the session scratchpad. qc.json has not been updated - the orchestrator owns that write.
